title: Erdős–Straus equation: an explicit exponent for the exceptional set and the Type II sieve sum; papers, Lean 4 formalization, verification code and engine runs
description:
Two papers on the Erdős–Straus equation 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z, with their sources and checks. Neither proves the Erdős–Straus conjecture, which remains open.

An explicit exponent for the exceptional set of the Erdős–Straus equation. The number of n <= N for which the equation has no solution is at most N exp(-(c1 - eps)(log N)^{2/3}) for every eps > 0 and all large N, where c1 = (3/2)((9/(8 pi^2))(40/49 - 6J + 6K))^{1/3}. Here J is an explicit double integral with 0 <= J < 0.000335 and K is the measure of the factorable pairs of the deep strips with K > 0.00859, both proved by computations in which every rounding error is directed against the bound, so that c1 > 0.6931; in closed form c1 >= (286983/(98560 pi^2))^{1/3} = 0.6657102497. A Monte Carlo simulation gives K = 0.0138 and c1 = 0.7015. Vaughan (1970) proved such a bound with no value of the constant. For the primes in the exceptional set, which satisfy n = 1 mod 24, the sieve of B. Dahan (arXiv:2608.24035) gives the constant 0.065, and 0.0943 with the constant of its sieve sum; T. Newton (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23760689) studies the exact divisor tests for the same primes, whose families are classes to fixed moduli. The residue classes come from the factorisations (p+1)/4 = u a alpha. Those in which one product of two factors is at most sqrt(p), the three corners of the triangle of factorisations, give exactly c0 = 9/(2^{8/3} pi^{2/3}) = 0.6607886973, and the paper proves that the large sieve gives no better exponent with them. The gain comes from the centre of the triangle: three strips of it are counted with Maynard's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli (Mem. AMS 306 (2025), no. 1542), and the deep strips behind them, to depth 1/10, with his second theorem on moduli up to p^{3/5} (no. 1543), by splitting each modulus into three factors of suitable sizes. The constructions were selected with the engine Anaxia of the BLLM project in three runs, two with version 3.0.5 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23469389) and one with version 3.1.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23484160). Version 4.0.1 corrects two estimates of the appendix, the error term of a hyperbola sum and the bound for the small variables in the adapted well-factorable estimate; the theorems and constants are unchanged.

A power-saving asymptotic for the two-parameter Type II sieve sum of the Erdős–Straus equation. The sum W(J) of 1/phi(4ua) over coprime pairs u, a <= J, which governs Dahan's sieve, equals (9/(2 pi^2))((log J + gamma + T)^2 + M) + O(J^{-1/2} log J) with explicit constants T and M. Its first two terms were found earlier by Z. Liu (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22650516); the constant term and the power-saving error are new.

preprintErdosStrausExceptionalSet/ and preprintErdosStrausSieveConstant/ hold the papers; exceptional/paper/ and paper/ their LaTeX sources with figures; dist/ the PDFs, LaTeX zips and arXiv tarballs; lean/ a Lean 4 and Mathlib project with 59 theorems (axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only); checks/ programs in C, C++, Python and Julia, among them the certified bounds for J and K; engine/ the records of the three engine runs and scripts that reproduce them; scripts/run_all.sh runs everything.
